direction-type.words: This chord occurs when the chromatic raising of the fifth in a major triad
or when the chromatic lowering of the root in a minor triad.
Augmented triad may appear as an auxiliary chord (including in the inversions).
This chord exists only in a major, because in a minor it is not possible
to chromatically raise the second degree of the scale.
You can use a dominant seventh augmented fifth chord as an auxiliary chord.
It can also be preceded by a triad or a sixth chord of the fourth degree of the scale.
For five voices, a similar alteration
of the ninth chord is possible.
